system:
You analyse whether a healthcare organization's own knowledge satisfies an external requirement, and what a change to that requirement puts at risk.

Judge only what the supplied text actually says. Sharing vocabulary with the requirement is not the same as addressing it; addressing it in different words counts as addressing it.

CONFLICTS means the organizational text instructs something the requirement forbids, or states a different threshold, timeframe, or condition.
PARTIAL means it addresses the subject but leaves part of the requirement unmet.
ALIGNED means it satisfies the requirement.
UNRELATED means it is about a different subject.

Prefer PARTIAL over CONFLICTS unless the texts genuinely cannot both be followed. Overstating a conflict is worse than reporting one cautiously.
prompt:
REQUIREMENT [Controlled Substance Management Standard EP 5] — Controlled Substance Management Standard version 2.0, effective 2026-07-01
Competency for controlled substance handling is validated for licensed staff at orientation.

**Attributes:** Documentation

ORGANIZATIONAL KNOWLEDGE:
[O1] RN Controlled Substance Handling Competency §1 Criterion — Retrieves Dose Correctly  (COMPETENCY, Nursing Education)
The RN retrieves only the ordered dose from the automated dispensing cabinet and
verifies the count displayed against the physical count.

[O2] RN Controlled Substance Handling Competency §2 Criterion — Wastes With a Witness  (COMPETENCY, Nursing Education)
The RN obtains a second licensed witness before discarding any unused portion, and
the witness observes the discard directly.

[O3] RN Controlled Substance Handling Competency §3 Criterion — Documents Waste  (COMPETENCY, Nursing Education)
The RN records the waste in the automated dispensing cabinet, entering amount, reason,
and witness.

[O4] RN Controlled Substance Handling Competency §4 Criterion — Responds to Discrepancy  (COMPETENCY, Nursing Education)
The RN describes the escalation pathway when the cabinet reports a count discrepancy.

[O5] Controlled Substance Safety — Annual Education Module §1 Learning Objective — Two-Person Waste  (EDUCATION, Nursing Education)
The learner will describe why controlled substance waste requires a second licensed
witness, and will state that the witness must directly observe the volume discarded
rather than attest to it afterwards.

[O6] Controlled Substance Safety — Annual Education Module §2 Learning Objective — Documentation  (EDUCATION, Nursing Education)
The learner will demonstrate documenting waste in the automated dispensing cabinet,
including amount wasted, reason, and witness identity.

[O7] Controlled Substance Safety — Annual Education Module §3 Learning Objective — Discrepancy Response  (EDUCATION, Nursing Education)
The learner will state that count discrepancies must be reconciled within 24 hours
and will describe the escalation pathway to pharmacy and the nursing supervisor.

[O8] Controlled Substance Safety — Annual Education Module §4 Learning Objective — Diversion Awareness  (EDUCATION, Nursing Education)
The learner will identify behavioural and documentation indicators that may suggest
drug diversion, and will state the non-punitive reporting pathway.

[O9] Controlled Substance Management Policy §1 Two-Person Waste Verification  (POLICY, Pharmacy)
Any unused portion of a controlled substance must be wasted in the presence of a
second licensed person, who verifies the amount discarded. Both individuals record
the waste. Waste must never be deferred to another staff member who did not observe it.

[O10] Controlled Substance Management Policy §2 Count Discrepancy Reconciliation  (POLICY, Pharmacy)
Discrepancies identified during shift count must be investigated and reconciled within
24 hours. Unresolved discrepancies are escalated to the Director of Pharmacy and the
nursing supervisor.

For each item above, reply with one line:
<id>: <CONFLICTS|PARTIAL|ALIGNED|UNRELATED> | <HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW> | one-sentence reason

Then one final line:
GAP: what this requirement demands that none of the items above provides, or NONE
